answers.label: Benefits and challenges of consequential methods
answers.text:
BENEFITS:
Workday aims to mitigate the carbon emissions of our global operations through a variety of procurement strategies. A consequential accounting framework allows more companies to engage in emissions reduction and procurement strategies in a transparent and impactful manner that will ultimately have the greatest net reduction in emissions.

Consequential accounting captures grid realities and assesses the marginal impact of a decision to increase or decrease consumption at a specific time and place. We believe this reflects the true footprint of corporate actions in a world where we all share the same atmosphere.

Attributional inventories, including LBM and MBM, do not measure impact. Their purpose is to accurately account for usage, as stated by GHGP (June 2025).

Consequential accounting will send the right investment signals to the market, with data guiding buyers to projects in regions where they will have the greatest impact. This allows companies operating in relatively low carbon grid regions to do more good by investing in clean energy from other regions, accelerating investment in areas with dirtier grids.

CHALLENGES:
Netting must be part of the calculus when considering emissions. Avoided emissions have the same impact as energy produced by renewables - less carbon in the atmosphere. An absolute number for avoided emissions is meaningless without comparing it to emissions caused by consumption.

Regarding additionality, we believe there must be a balance—if it is too stringent, it will deter investment in impactful projects, too loose and we miss out on the opportunity to push towards a carbon-free grid.

answers.label: Appropriateness of the TWG subgroup formula
Why the formula is or is not appropriate
answers.text:
We appreciate the progress made on the consequential metric using marginal emissions rates. However, the formula as provided does not achieve what is needed for Impact Accounting to be useful to reporting entities. This is primarily because it is currently only applicable to emissions avoided by procurement, and does not calculate or allow the netting of emissions caused by consumption. The ability to calculate emissions caused AND avoided is a pre-requisite for the impact accounting option to have any material utility for reporting entities. [1],[2]

This is important for organizations, like Workday, that invest in renewable contracts in areas that have more carbon-intensive grids. Netting would allow Workday to more accurately measure our emissions impact between our avoided emissions and our load.

It should also be noted that it is our understanding that this formula does not represent what the TWG consequential subgroup proposed, which includes netting.[3]

[1] WattTime: Accounting for Impact, https://watttime.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/WattTime-AccountingForImpact-202209-vFinal2.pdf

[2] RE-Source: Carbon Matching, https://www.emissionsfirst.com/_files/ugd/820a9e_23bdd35c3c65419a9501ceaf32cc1d40.pdf

[3] Public Statement from Members of the GHG Protocol Scope 2 TWG Consequential Subgroup, November 2025, https://marginalimpactmethod.org/
